title: Close Out a Day That Had Exceptions
scenario: It is 7:00 AM on the messy morning. Delivery and retention still happen - but a day with exceptions has a third closeout job: making sure the exceptions were routed to their owners, on the record. A dropped row nobody follows up on becomes next month's mystery.
input:
Closeout runbook, morning brief:
- At 7:00 AM the brief is sent to the Trading Desk DL and archived to briefs-archive (retention 30 days). The archive seeds tomorrow's baseline.
- On exception days, the run record must also list each exception and confirm it was reported to the owner of upstream data quality, the Risk Desk Lead.
- Today's exceptions: the MISO feed row was dropped at cleaning (missing settled value); WAUE was excluded from variance (no forecast).
instructions: Record the standard delivery and retention facts.
List both exception hubs and confirm who they were reported to.
Mark that the archive seeds tomorrow's baseline.
Return one JSON object - the run record - then validate.
copilotPrompt: Write an exception-aware closeout record as JSON with deliveredTo, sendTime, archiveFolder, retentionDays, droppedRowHub, missingForecastHub, exceptionsReportedTo, and seedsTomorrowBaseline, based on this runbook.
successMessage: Day closed out. Delivered, retained, seeded - and every exception is in somebody's queue instead of nobody's memory.

intro.heading: Before you build: exception days close differently

sections.title: The third closeout job
sections.body: Quiet days close with delivery and retention. Exception days add routing: each anomaly must reach the person who can fix its cause. The MISO row is a vendor conversation; the WAUE gap is a model change - both belong to the Risk Desk Lead's queue, and the run record proves they got there.

sections.title: Tomorrow inherits today, gaps included
sections.body: Tonight's archive seeds tomorrow's baseline - and note what that means for MISO: dropped today means no clean MISO price in the archive, so tomorrow MISO may have a baseline gap of its own. Exceptions propagate through the loop; the closeout record is where that becomes visible.

sections.title: One record, both audiences
sections.body: The auditor reads this record to confirm the exceptions were handled; tomorrow's operator reads it to know what today left behind. Same fields serve both - which is the mark of a well-designed record.

fieldGuide.meaning: The hub whose feed row was dropped.
Who owns following up on both.
fieldGuide.hint: The owner of upstream data quality.

fieldGuide.meaning: Whether this archive is tomorrow's baseline.

takeaway.heading: Exception day closed
points: You closed the loop with all three jobs: delivered, retained, and routed the exceptions to their owner.
The run record names both anomalies and their recipient - follow-up is now a queue item, not a memory.
You saw exceptions propagate through the loop: today's dropped MISO row is tomorrow's potential baseline gap.
Across this tier you handled the whole exception lifecycle: detect (cleaning), behave honestly (variance), surface (brief), route (here).
The workflow can now finish a messy day as cleanly as a quiet one - with nothing lost and nothing hidden.
